text:
Ivy: quick heads-up — new user hit a bundling error on Netlify edge: "Cannot find module 'redwood-js-sdk'" when using next-edge adapter.
Marcus: ouch. netlify/edge likes pure ESM imports. Are we accidentally shipping a CJS main that tooling picks?
Talia: our package.json still lacks an exports map. many bundlers fall back to main -> cjs.
Ben: also noticed our ESM build for edge pulled in a tiny helper that uses process.hrtime.bigint() — not available on some edge runtimes.
Ivy: so two problems: resolution (exports) and runtime-safety in ESM entry.
Marcus: short fix: add explicit exports with an "/edge" subpath pointing to a minimal edge-entry.mjs that only uses web APIs.
Talia: agree. and keep top-level "types": "dist/types/index.d.ts" so TS consumers resolve types. don't put types inside exports.
Ben: build fix: stop fully bundling auth retry into both outputs. extract auth/core.ts -> dist/auth/core.mjs and import from both bundles so retry logic is identical. avoid setImmediate; use setTimeout fallback.
Ivy: for onboarding immediate workaround I'll patch the sample with a guard: const isEdge = typeof globalThis?.fetch === 'function' && process.env.NETLIFY === 'true'; const sdk = await import(isEdge ? 'redwood-js-sdk/edge' : 'redwood-js-sdk');
Marcus: add a CI smoke job that runs the sample under a headless edge runner (wrangler or netlify dev). that'll catch these regressions.
Talia: I'll open PR for exports + edge-entry. Ben can handle refactor of auth/core in build. Marcus will add CI. Ivy will update sample and README.
BuildBot: queued job devex/edge-smoke for the PRs.
Ivy: thanks — this should cut onboarding friction for edge consumers. will follow up when PRs land.
